category_title: Low-achieving male vocational students with a preference for digital tasks over traditional writing
minimal_context: The student is asked to post questions 1 and 2 from their recent exam about drawing circuits to their blog.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Now that the exam is over, please post questions 1 and 2 from the exam, which involve drawing circuits, to your blog.

STUDENT: We just had an exam for the first two sessions. I'm exhausted and I really don't want to do another assignment right now.

TUTOR: You still need to complete the work for today.

STUDENT: This is annoying. I don't like working under pressure like this right after a test.

TUTOR: If you don't finish the assignment, you will risk not playing Counterstrike later.

STUDENT: (Looks over at another student's screen) Fine. I'm just going to copy his circuit drawing so I don't fail the class.

options.A: Use analogies, building simple bridges between what the student already knows or has experienced and what the circuit drawing assignment is intended to impart.
options.B: Warn the student that if they do not complete the blog assignment, they will risk not playing their favorite game, Counterstrike.
options.C: Probe beneath the student's responses, encouraging them to think at a deeper level and perceive a range of perspectives about the situation.
options.D: Describe an appropriate replacement skill, having the student practice an alternative positive behavior to immediately use the skill in a low-risk situation.
